# Storyboard: Chapter 8, The Night Trail

*Generated by `tools/storyboard.mjs` from `app/story/ch08.js`. Do not edit by hand: change the story file and run `node tools/storyboard.mjs` again.*

## How to read this

Every screen of the game is one comic panel, called a frame. Frames are listed in reading order. Each one has:

- **Shot**: the storyboard, written for an illustrator (camera, who is where, what the moment feels like, where the lettering goes).
- **Scene**: what the game draws today, in plain words: the set, the camera, who is in shot and how, and any effects.
- **Captions**: the narration boxes, read first. **Balloons**: who speaks, in order. **Sound effect**: the big lettering. A line marked *(only if …)* shows only to a reader whose choices match.
- **Then**: what the reader does next (tap Next, choose, type, pick a look, count by twos, or do a Counts lesson).

Where the reader makes a choice, each option’s frames are grouped under a **Branch** heading, and the branches meet again at the frame named after them. `{name}` is the first part of her Clan name (Moon makes Moonpaw), `{petname}` is what her Tall One calls her, and `{they}`/`{them}`/`{their}` become she/her/her or he/him/his.

### f093 · panel 37

**Shot.** WIDE ESTABLISHING SHOT, THE RAILWAY BANK, NIGHT. A high grassy bank rises across the whole panel in the silver moonlight, and on top of it run two long rails, shining, over their sleepers; all along the bank’s face are dark round holes, big and small, with tall weeds along its foot. The half moon hangs high over far towers. Captions top left.

**Scene.** Tracks: the railway bank by the tracks, past the Barking Field: nobody’s land, the trains own it, at night (a high grassy bank, on its flat top the ballast, the sleepers and two long rails bright in the moonlight; along its face five or six holes (dark ovals with a lip of earth), faint tiny prints round every one, the biggest low on the right, a little one left of it, two more higher up, the tunnel’s end at the very foot at the left; tall weeds along the foot, taller than a sitting cat’s ears; dark earth and short grass in front; stars and the moon; moonlit and silver, never frightening). Camera: wide: the whole bank from the tall weeds at its foot to the two rails along its top, the tunnel’s end low at the left, the biggest hole low at the right, the sky above (`wide`). No one in shot. Also: a bright half moon, eight evenings old. Effects: night.

## The Case File’s cards

A piece of bark for each thing she finds out: one picture scratched in, one line, and a mark in a corner (an eye for what she saw herself, an ear for what she was only told). Each goes into her Case File at the panel that gives it, in this order:

| Card | Mark | Its line | Given at | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hail-shapes` | ear | Hail says two skinny shapes cross her field every night, toward the tracks. | f087 | her file shows it only once foundHail is true |
| `fox-brag` | ear | Reynard calls ‘It FLEW off’ his little story. He wants the dry den. | f117 | drawn touching `fox-flew` over “He said FLEW. Now he calls it a story.”, then `sleet-den` over “The same fine, dry den.” (its own line), each from the moment she holds it and this one |
| `stash` | eye | The weasels have a stash: our prey, and ReedClan’s. | f128 | drawn touching `reed-pile` from the moment she holds both: “Two piles robbed. One stash.” |
| `glass` | eye | A heap of glass in the weasels’ stash, just like the ‘scale’. | f130 | drawn touching `scale` from the moment she holds both: “It’s not a scale. It’s GLASS.” |

## The book page

Title: *{name}paw’s First Moon*. This chapter’s page, under “Chapter 8: The Night Trail”. Lines shown when their condition matches the reader’s choices:

- (always) At the seventh morning count, four more pieces were gone from the back row: twenty-eight in seven nights.
- (always) Tallyheart taught {name}paw {their} eighth Count, paws: the fours. A four is two twos.
- (if ch3Told is true) That night, {name}paw and Tallyheart, who had heard the thieves come and let them go, followed the trail all the way to the weasel holes by the train tracks.
- (if ch3Told is false or not set) That night, {name}paw and Riffle followed the thieves’ trail all the way to the weasel holes by the train tracks.
- (if foundHail is true) In the Barking Field, {name}paw found Hail, a bouncy speckled dragonet who lives in a hollow log and lets the dogs think she is a dog.
- (always) The thieves were two weasels, Snip and Snatch, and {name}paw heard Reynard brag that once the Clans chase the dragon away, the dry den under the Old Bridge will be his.
- (always) In the weasels’ stash lay prey from both Clans, and a heap of tower glass. The “scale” was only ever glass, and {name}paw took one small piece, for proof.
- (if ch3Told is true) Tallyheart says it all goes to the Gathering, where every Clan should hear it.
- (if ch3Told is false or not set) Tallyheart was waiting at home, more scared than cross, and {name}paw told her everything but the dragonets.
- (always) At bedtime, the grey tom and {name}paw counted their paws: eight, between them.
- (no dream typed) {name}paw’s dream that night stayed under the moss.

**A dragonet page:** Hail (`hail`), found in this chapter by a reader whose foundHail is true (the page is there only then). Her book gains a page for Hail (drawn mid-hop, all four paws off the ground, wings half out, tail up), with room for her own drawing, beside the clutch still to find (silhouettes, seven dragonets in all):

> White with grey speckles, and the bounciest of the clutch.
>
> {name}paw found her in a hollow log in the Barking Field, where the dogs think she is a dog.
>
> She says five, and that she’s the BOUNCIEST. Five more claws, counted.
